mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of tighter policy compressing equity discount rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: FED Funds rate above 4% in late-cycle tightening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during such FEDFUNDS spikes (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not spike in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, labor market slack increases, boosting consumer confidence and driving a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite UNRATE remaining below 4% for two months, or the two-month UNRATE decline is not confirmed by other labor indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (household spending index) above 1.5% of the prior month's level predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals strengthening consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST grows > 1.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such HOUST growth (p > 0.05), or the pattern reverses in the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) by more than 5% in the prior quarter is associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects supply-side contraction and reduced market optimism.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 5% from Q1 to Q2 in the prior quarter
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative during such INDPRO declines (p > 0.05), or INDPRO recovers strongly in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise simultaneously by at least 0.25% in the same month, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to anticipated inflationary tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS up ≥ 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL up ≥ 0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when both proxies move in the specified direction, or the joint effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) of at least 2,000 for three months indicates labor market expansion, leading to a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases ≥ 2,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such labor expansion (p > 0.05), or the expansion pattern is not confirmed by other labor indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in GDPC1 (GDP chain) followed by a rebound above the prior pre-recession trend line predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates economic stabilization.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two months then crosses above pre-2008 trend line
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative or flat during the pattern, or GDPC1 does not show the described rebound.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 10% in a month compared to the prior month, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to weak demand and supply-side weakness.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such RSAFS declines (p > 0.05), or the decline is not confirmed by other supply indicators.
